records.found: Nothing new about his own case. A paper in GeroScience dated 2026-11-05 bears on the argument he made for fifteen years: in about 11,500 kidney transplant recipients followed a median of 11 years, those prescribed rapamycin did not live longer than those who were not. It is an observational study of sick people on other immune-suppressing drugs, so it counts against without settling anything.

findings.what: Stewart and Fitzsimmons, GeroScience (peer-reviewed paper, abstract read): among United States kidney transplant recipients alive with a working graft at one year, 4,885 prescribed rapamycin and 6,589 not, followed a median of 11 years, median age at death was 64.6 against 64.3 years after adjustment (95% interval for the difference -1.6 to 2.0 years); the authors saw no meaningful gain in long-term survival.

unmatched.what: A new trial was registered: VITAL-H (NCT07923630), University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio with the United States Department of Health and Human Services as collaborator. It plans 1,200 people on dapagliflozin, oral semaglutide or placebo for 36 months to test whether two approved drugs delay age-related decline in health and function; not yet recruiting, start planned for 2027-01, main results 2030-12.
unmatched.why_it_matters: A large, publicly backed trial with healthy ageing itself as the aim, using approved drugs; it is the kind of trial the measuring question has been waiting for. Not found in the records.

unmatched.what: Stewart and Fitzsimmons, GeroScience: in 4,885 kidney transplant recipients prescribed rapamycin and 6,589 not, followed a median of 11 years, adjusted median age at death was 64.6 against 64.3 years; no meaningful survival gain from long-term rapamycin.
unmatched.why_it_matters: A result that counts against rapamycin lengthening human life, from one of the largest sets of people on the drug for years; it belongs beside the rapamycin treatment entry and may bear on its estimate. Not found in the records.

unmatched.what: A new trial was registered: NCT07912164, Human Biome S.A., a placebo-controlled trial in 68 adults aged 45 to 80 of capsules of gut bacteria from donors, with the pace-of-ageing clock DunedinPACE as its main measure; not yet recruiting.
unmatched.why_it_matters: A trial that uses a blood clock as its main outcome, which is the measuring branch's open question in practice.
